scope.content_policy: All businesses, people, events, products, prices, schedules and statistics below are fictional or demo data. No external research, user testing or real client relationship is claimed.

dimensions: poster, package, sign, ticket, program and display formats
editorial, navigational, menu, event and community tasks
visual systems driven by grid, hierarchy, character, pictography, rhythm, modularity or spatial orientation
diversity_plan.excluded_adjacent_scope: This is a set of unrelated real-world design commissions, not a researched visual special (B04), a ten-screen product journey (B05), or ten everyday information problems (B06).

shared_documentation.role: Service syntax boundary and version caveat
Constraint, flex, stack and overflow planning
Decoration, transform, clipping and filter planning
Typography, wrapping, baseline and inline content planning
Previously obtained installed-font list; actual rendering still pending

cases.title: Ember Alley Night Market menu
cases.audience: Hungry evening visitors aged 18-45 moving quickly through a dense outdoor night market
cases.use_context: Printed A2 menu board beside a fictional street-food stall; viewed from 1-3 metres in mixed neon light with limited reading time
cases.user_goal: Find a preferred dish, understand price and dietary markers, and order without asking the vendor to repeat every option

content_basis.label: FICTIONAL_DEMO
content_basis.description: Invented Ember Alley stall and demo menu: six skewers, three rice bowls and three drinks, with clearly fictional prices and allergen symbols. No real stall or menu was surveyed.

cases.visual_intent: Use a dark ember-red field, an oversized category axis, compact price rails and a custom geometric skewer motif; keep the visual heat in the header while making menu scanning calm and direct.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: At final full-size view, all nine item names, all prices and the three category headings are visible and unclipped.
completion_criteria.check_method: Inspect full PNG and menu regions at 100%; reconcile item and price count against the brief.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Dietary marker meanings are printed as text and remain distinguishable without relying on red/green alone.
completion_criteria.check_method: Zoom each legend and marker; compare shape plus label against the planned legend.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: The three food categories and two drink categories form five visibly separate reading bands with consistent price alignment.
completion_criteria.check_method: Full-image and column-alignment visual review; compare repeated row positions.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: The footer identifies the concept as a fictional demo rather than implying a real operating vendor.
completion_criteria.check_method: Read footer at 100% and verify demo label presence.

criteria_history.reason: Initial criteria fixed before the first Snapshot render request.

cases.independence_rationale: A fast, outdoor, transaction-oriented menu is the only B01 case organised around rapid item selection and price comparison; its dense row system and stall-scale typography differ from every other audience and task.

cases.title: Afterlight Museum exhibition identity
cases.audience: Museum visitors and cultural audiences considering an exhibition about fictional nocturnal landscapes
cases.use_context: Large foyer poster and adjacent lift-lobby reproduction; viewed first at 3-8 metres, then approached for dates and interpretation
cases.user_goal: Recognise the exhibition identity, feel its conceptual tone, and learn where, when and how to visit

content_basis.label: FICTIONAL_DEMO
content_basis.description: Invented Afterlight Museum and demo exhibition 'A Field Guide to Midnight'; invented dates, gallery location, curator note and admission information.

cases.visual_intent: Build an editorial identity around a cropped DSL moon-disc, a thin horizon and a restrained serif/sans pairing; let negative space and scale establish cultural authority rather than promotional urgency.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: The title, venue, dates and gallery location are readable at final full size and correctly grouped.
completion_criteria.check_method: Full image plus detail crops; compare text against planned exhibition facts.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Moon, horizon and title overlap intentionally without hiding any letter or leaving ambiguous accidental collisions.
completion_criteria.check_method: Inspect title-to-disc and disc-to-horizon intersections at 100%.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: The composition retains a quiet focal area and at least two levels of viewing hierarchy from distance to detail.
completion_criteria.check_method: Review a downscaled thumbnail and the final-size image side by side.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: No element crosses the 48 px intended poster safe margin or is clipped by the canvas.
completion_criteria.check_method: Overlay/reference safe bounds during detail inspection and confirm all four edges.

criteria_history.reason: Initial criteria fixed before the first Snapshot render request.

cases.independence_rationale: This is a long-distance institutional identity with contemplative pacing, not a sales menu; it relies on spatial minimalism and two-stage reading rather than dense listings or instructions.

cases.title: Last Bus Cinema double-bill poster
cases.audience: Independent-film fans browsing a fictional repertory cinema programme
cases.use_context: Portrait poster in a cinema window and a smaller A3 lobby print; read in a few seconds while walking
cases.user_goal: Understand the double bill, its genre atmosphere, screening time and ticket call-to-action

content_basis.label: FICTIONAL_DEMO
content_basis.description: Invented films 'The Quiet Frequency' and 'Platform Nine, Nowhere', invented director names, fictional screening date/time and invented cinema Last Bus Cinema.

cases.visual_intent: Use an off-register two-panel composition suggesting interrupted film frames, with condensed uppercase type, a ticket-like time block and a limited cobalt/cream/acid palette.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Both film titles, the double-bill relationship, date, time, venue and demo ticket line are present and legible.
completion_criteria.check_method: Text inventory and full-size/detail visual inspection.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Rotated panels create deliberate tension but no title, ticket line or key credit is obscured or cut off.
completion_criteria.check_method: Inspect all transformed edges at 100% and compare computed bounds with canvas and safe area.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: The screening block is discoverable in a thumbnail and uses stronger contrast than secondary credits.
completion_criteria.check_method: Downscale to phone size, then verify local contrast in the final PNG.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: The image explicitly identifies its programme content as fictional demo material.
completion_criteria.check_method: Check footer copy at 100%.

criteria_history.reason: Initial criteria fixed before the first Snapshot render request.

cases.independence_rationale: A promotional image for a time-sensitive cultural screening uses cinematic montage and tilted typography; it is neither a museum identity nor a practical information sign.

cases.title: Hush Room recital programme cover
cases.audience: Chamber-music subscribers, performers and attentive listeners
cases.use_context: A5 printed programme handed out before a fictional intimate recital; read seated under warm hall lighting
cases.user_goal: Follow the running order, identify works and performers, and know when applause is expected

content_basis.label: FICTIONAL_DEMO
content_basis.description: Invented Hush Room recital with four original-sounding but fictional work titles, invented composers/arrangers and demo performers; fictional timings and interval.

cases.visual_intent: Treat the programme as a quiet musical score: a narrow vertical duration spine, measured horizontal rules, serif titles and generous margins; use page-like asymmetry rather than poster graphics.
cases.medium: A5 chamber recital programme cover and running order
dsl_capabilities: tabular numeric alignment through fixed columns

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Four works, invented creator credits, performers, timings, interval and venue are complete and readable.
completion_criteria.check_method: Compare the rendered text inventory against the case's planned content table.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: All duration labels share a stable alignment and no row wraps into the next work.
completion_criteria.check_method: Inspect row baselines and duration column at 100%; verify text has finite widths.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Mixed Latin names and numeric timings show no missing glyphs, overlap or accidental clipping.
completion_criteria.check_method: Zoom every mixed-script line and inspect fallback rendering.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Interval and applause cue are visually distinct but not louder than the running order.
completion_criteria.check_method: Thumbnail hierarchy review and detail review of cue labels.

criteria_history.reason: Initial criteria fixed before the first Snapshot render request.

cases.independence_rationale: This case supports sequential, seated reading of a performance order; its score-like tabular typography and small-print programme function are unlike the public-facing cinema and museum posters.

cases.title: Common Clay workshop enrolment postcard
cases.audience: Local adults looking for a small, welcoming first ceramics experience
cases.use_context: A6 postcard distributed through a fictional community centre and arts-shop counter; handled at close range
cases.user_goal: Understand the beginner level, session price, materials, accessibility and how to reserve a place

content_basis.label: FICTIONAL_DEMO
content_basis.description: Invented Common Clay studio, beginner workshop title, fictional tutor, dates, prices, capacity and reservation code; no real workshop or booking system is represented.

cases.visual_intent: Use tactile-looking DSL clay bands, an irregular but bounded vessel silhouette, friendly oversized numbering and a tear-off-style reservation strip; avoid the solemnity of the recital programme.
cases.medium: A6 enrolment postcard, front and back information combined in one proof

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Workshop title, level, two fictional dates, price, capacity and reservation method are visible and internally consistent.
completion_criteria.check_method: Reconcile rendered copy with the demo content plan and inspect at A6-equivalent scale.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: The vessel motif frames rather than overlaps essential text and does not introduce an accidental cropping edge.
completion_criteria.check_method: Inspect path bounds and all text-to-motif intersections.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: The reservation strip reads as a distinct actionable area with a clear fictional code and no fake interactive claim.
completion_criteria.check_method: Thumbnail review followed by 100% inspection of the strip.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Body and small print remain readable in a grayscale print simulation.
completion_criteria.check_method: Convert a temporary review copy to grayscale outside the final artifact path and inspect contrast.

criteria_history.reason: Initial criteria fixed before the first Snapshot render request.

cases.independence_rationale: A tactile, close-range enrolment postcard solves a personal booking decision and combines a friendly craft identity with practical small print, unlike any large public poster in this set.

cases.title: Riverside flood-response door notice
cases.audience: Residents, including older people and readers of English or simplified Chinese
cases.use_context: A3 weather-resistant notice posted at a fictional apartment entrance during a drill; glanced at while preparing to leave
cases.user_goal: Immediately recognise the drill status, know the safe action and find the correct assembly point and assistance contact

content_basis.label: FICTIONAL_DEMO
content_basis.description: Entirely invented flood-preparedness drill for fictional Riverside House; fictional assembly point, floor wardens, time and demonstration phone number. This is a design mock-up, not live emergency guidance.

cases.visual_intent: Use a strict warning header, three oversized action steps, bilingual parallel lines and a high-contrast location panel; prioritise comprehension over atmosphere and label the mock-up prominently.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: DRILL / 演练 is the first readable message and the notice is unmistakably labelled fictional.
completion_criteria.check_method: Inspect thumbnail and header detail; confirm no live-emergency implication.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Exactly three actions appear in numbered order, each with equivalent English and simplified Chinese meaning.
completion_criteria.check_method: Bilingual copy review and visual sequence check; no claim of certified translation.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Assembly point, drill time, wardens and demonstration assistance contact are grouped and readable at intended print size.
completion_criteria.check_method: Print-scale visual check and text inventory.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: No instruction depends on colour alone, and all Chinese glyphs render without missing-character boxes.
completion_criteria.check_method: Grayscale review and glyph inspection at 200%.

criteria_history.reason: Initial criteria fixed before the first Snapshot render request.

cases.independence_rationale: The only high-stakes operational notice in B01, designed for rapid bilingual comprehension under stress; its goal is correct action rather than persuasion, attendance or brand expression.

cases.title: Juniper Ridge trailhead orientation sign
cases.audience: Hikers with varying experience, including first-time visitors and readers who need large labels
cases.use_context: Fictional trailhead sign seen outdoors in variable daylight, often while wearing gloves or standing several metres away
cases.user_goal: Choose a suitable route, understand distance, climb and expected time, and identify hazards before setting off

content_basis.label: FICTIONAL_DEMO
content_basis.description: Invented Juniper Ridge reserve with three demo loop routes, fictional distances, elevation gains and durations, plus invented trail symbols and safety notes. No real map or geographic claim is made.

cases.visual_intent: Organise the sign as a physical decision panel with three route cards, a bold pictographic trail spine, terrain bands and a large north/orientation marker; use labels as well as colour coding.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Three routes show matching names, distance, climb, duration and difficulty labels with no swapped values.
completion_criteria.check_method: Compare each card to a planned route table and inspect column alignment.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Route pictograms and written difficulty remain meaningful in grayscale and at thumbnail scale.
completion_criteria.check_method: Grayscale and downscaled review; verify no colour-only distinctions.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: A 'You are here' marker, north indicator, hazard note and fictional reserve label are unambiguous.
completion_criteria.check_method: Inspect spatial relationships and copy at 100%.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: The sign is explicitly a demonstration concept and cannot be mistaken for deployed wayfinding.
completion_criteria.check_method: Read demo label and footer in final PNG.

criteria_history.reason: Initial criteria fixed before the first Snapshot render request.

cases.independence_rationale: A spatially anchored, outdoor decision system helps users choose a physical route; its multi-column comparison and environmental legibility differ from the bilingual door notice and indoor menus.

cases.title: Little Archive seed-library package series
cases.audience: Home growers and community seed-library members choosing packets to borrow or sow
cases.use_context: A coordinated set of three small paper seed envelopes on a fictional library shelf; picked up and read at 15-30 cm
cases.user_goal: Distinguish varieties, check sowing season and packet status, and understand the return/relabel process

content_basis.label: FICTIONAL_DEMO
content_basis.description: Invented Little Archive library and three fictional varieties: 'Cloud Parsnip', 'Amber Dwarf Bean' and 'Windowbox Coriander'; invented packet years and demo sowing guidance.

cases.visual_intent: Create a modular family of envelopes with distinct botanical line motifs generated in DSL, archival numbering, crop-specific colour fields and a consistent status band; diversity comes from the crop system rather than three unrelated layouts.
cases.medium: Coordinated set of three seed-packet package fronts

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Three complete, distinct packet fronts are shown with variety, packet year, sowing window and library status for each.
completion_criteria.check_method: Packet-by-packet text inventory against the planned demo table.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Shared alignment, status band and typography make the packets a family while crop motifs distinguish them at a glance.
completion_criteria.check_method: Compare common edges and review the set as a thumbnail.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: The decorative pattern is clearly not represented as a functional scannable code.
completion_criteria.check_method: Inspect label next to the pattern and avoid machine-readable encoding claims.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Small sowing and return instructions remain legible without collisions or clipping.
completion_criteria.check_method: Inspect each packet's lower region at 200%.

criteria_history.reason: Initial criteria fixed before the first Snapshot render request.

cases.independence_rationale: The only package-system case, designed for close-range identification and repeated shelf recognition across a product family; its controlled modular variation is not counted as three independent cases.

cases.title: Signal Break arena bracket display
cases.audience: Fictional esports event attendees and competitors following a live tournament
cases.use_context: Widescreen screen above a fictional competition stage and mirrored on a lobby display; read from a distance with rapid updates implied but not animated
cases.user_goal: See which teams have advanced, where the next match is, and when the final begins

content_basis.label: FICTIONAL_DEMO
content_basis.description: Invented Signal Break invitational with eight fictional team names, invented scores, stage labels and final time. The static proof represents one demo bracket state only.

cases.visual_intent: Turn the bracket into a bold horizontal circuit: four feeder columns converge on a central final node, with electric line motifs, dark surfaces and large status numerals; favour at-a-glance advancement over dense statistics.
dsl_capabilities: Container gradients and glows via boxShadow

completion_criteria.observable_condition: The static bracket contains eight unique fictional teams, coherent advancement from four opening matches to two semifinals to one final, and no orphan result.
completion_criteria.check_method: Trace every connector and reconcile teams and scores against the planned demo bracket.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Winners, upcoming match and final time can be identified in a 480 px-wide thumbnail.
completion_criteria.check_method: Downscale to lobby thumbnail and inspect status hierarchy.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Connector lines terminate at the correct team rows without crossing labels or implying a different pairing.
completion_criteria.check_method: Inspect connector geometry at 100% and trace each path visually.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: A visible label identifies the bracket as a fictional static demo state.
completion_criteria.check_method: Read header/footer label in the final image.

criteria_history.reason: Initial criteria fixed before the first Snapshot render request.

cases.independence_rationale: The only large-screen competitive data display, with branching relationships and a single live-state snapshot; its wide circuit geometry and rapid-read requirement distinguish it from printed signs and intimate publications.

cases.title: Fieldwork Architecture project hoarding
cases.audience: Passers-by, prospective clients and neighbours curious about a fictional building project
cases.use_context: Temporary construction-site hoarding on a fictional civic lane; read while walking at varying angles and later photographed close-up
cases.user_goal: Understand what is being built, the project's public value, the responsible fictional practice and when the site will reopen

content_basis.label: FICTIONAL_DEMO
content_basis.description: Invented Fieldwork Architecture and fictional 'Lantern Yard Community Rooms' project; original DSL-built axonometric concept drawing, invented project facts and demo completion window. Not a real architectural proposal.

cases.visual_intent: Combine a precise axonometric DSL drawing, a huge project-name grid, a materials legend and a public-benefit strip; use the measured language of architecture to make a temporary construction barrier feel intentional and informative.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Project name, fictional practice, community purpose, site status and demo reopening window are present and readable.
completion_criteria.check_method: Copy inventory and full-size/detail review.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: The axonometric building reads as one coherent structure with aligned floors, roof and three labelled public spaces.
completion_criteria.check_method: Trace shared axes in the final PNG and compare label anchors to geometry.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Technical linework stays subordinate to the project title and does not become visual noise at thumbnail size.
completion_criteria.check_method: Full-size and downscaled comparison.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: The hoarding labels the concept and building as fictional rather than presenting it as approved work.
completion_criteria.check_method: Inspect concept-demo caption and footer.

criteria_history.reason: Initial criteria fixed before the first Snapshot render request.

cases.independence_rationale: A public-facing architectural hoarding combines spatial illustration, technical explanation and construction communication; it is the only B01 case whose main visual is an invented built form rather than type, packaging or interface-like panels.
